events.label: Nitehawk: The Devils — Recent Restorations
events.desc: Starring: Vanessa Redgrave, Oliver Reed, Dudley Sutton, Max Adrian, Gemma Jones, Murray Melvin 4K restoration Ken Russell’s controversial adaptation of Aldous Huxley’s The Devils of Loudun is at long last available in its full, provocative splendor. This new restoration thrillingly incorporates material that was originally censored—footage that Russell deemed some of the best and most political work of his career. A young Derek Jarman designed the sets that house this story of a vengeful nun (Vanessa Redgrave) who accuses a priest (Oliver Reed) of collaborating with the devil, resulting in the apparent possession of an entire convent. A fearless account of state and church corruption, The Devils mixes graphic sexual imagery with religious iconography in an unforgettable spectacle that could only issue from the mind of Ken Russell. Following its NYFF64 premiere, The Devils will open on 35mm for a one-week engagement beginning October 16 at Film at Lincoln Center. A Warner Bros. Clockwork release. (Directed by Ken Russell, 1971, 114 min., DCP, Rated NC-17.) Film series: Recent Restorations / The Anniversary Party / Brunch Movies. Tickets at nitehawkcinema.com.

events.label: Nitehawk: Castle in the Sky — 35mm Screenings
events.desc: Starring: Anna Paquin, James Van Der Beek, Cloris Leachman, Mark Hamill, Mandy Patinkin Castle in the Sky is a timeless story of courage and friendship, with stunning animation from acclaimed Academy Award-winning director Hayao Miyazaki. This high-flying adventure begins when Pazu, an engineer’s apprentice, spies a young girl, Sheeta, floating down from the sky, held aloft by a glowing pendant. Both Sheeta and Pazu are searching for the legendary floating castle, Laputa, and they vow to travel there together to unravel the mystery of the luminous crystal. But their quest won’t be easy, as soon they are being pursued by greedy air pirates, the military, and secret government agents, who all seek the power Sheeta alone can control. (Directed by Hayao Miyazaki, 1986, 124 min., 35mm, Rated PG.) Film series: 35mm Screenings / Family Friendly / Nostalgia, Ultra. / The Anniversary Party / Brunch Movies. Tickets at nitehawkcinema.com.

events.label: Nitehawk: NoBudge Live 53 — Shorts
events.desc: NoBudge is happy to present a program of eight short films from a group of emerging indie filmmakers mostly based in New York. The lineup focuses on narrative dramas and comedies exploring a range of styles and tones. Six of the films are NYC or Brooklyn premieres and all filmmakers will be in attendance for a post-screening Q&A and Afterparty. NoBudge is an online platform spotlighting the best in low-budget indie filmmaking. “One of the best places to sample what’s happening in low-budget cinema worldwide,” says Glenn Kenny of The New York Times. Its mission is to provide a supportive home for emerging indie filmmakers working with limited resources and without major industry connections, and to be a trusted discovery platform. All My Idols are Fat NYC Premiere . Director Neha Simon in person. Two friends stumble into finding out how close their relationship really is. (12 min) Plastic Glass Brooklyn Premiere. Director Mitchell Clark in person. Careening through a day in the life of a high schooler, a teenager and his friends experiment with a mysterious drug-like substance. (15 min) Behind this Locked Door Director Matthew Brennan in person. When a woman moves in with her boyfriend, she discovers he spends a concerning amount of time in the bathroom. (13 min) Period Piece Brooklyn Premiere. Director Flora Nolan in person. When her period abruptly stops, a young woman reckons with her body and reflects on her expectations of womanhood. (12 min) Making Love Songs Brooklyn Premiere . Directors Leon and Daniel Brodsky in person. A teenager is commissioned to photograph a series of disturbing events. (17 min) Faux Amis NYC Premiere. Director Theodore Matza in person. Two twenty-somethings travel to Paris so that one of them can connect with an Instagram boyfriend. (15 min) Fix Director Vogue Giambri in person. Do you run around late at night looking for your fix? (15 min) Whoa NYC Premiere. Director Elizabeth O’Donnell in person. A baby-boomer mom and her millennial daughter take psilocybin mushrooms together. (13 min) (2026, 112 min., DCP.) Film series: Shorts. Tickets at nitehawkcinema.com.

events.label: Nitehawk: The Thing — 35mm Screenings
events.desc: Starring: Kurt Russell, Wilford Brimley, Keith David, David Clennon, T.K. Carter Snuggle up! Kurt Russell battles against the cold and a mysterious alien life-form in the John Carpenter version of The Thing . A team of scientists working in the frozen landscape of the Antarctic encounter a shape-shifting and killer alien being after a strange dog enters the camp. This is, of course, after witnessing a Norwegian team chasing the dog to kill it but perish in a helicopter crash before they can and before they can explain. Isolated in a part of the world nearly as remote as space, Kurt Russell’s R.J. MacReady leads the charge for survival not just his team but for the entire human race. Overshadowed upon its release by the more family friendly film E.T., Carpenter’s The Thing is a terrifying look at outer space in our own world that combines brilliant special effects and humorously scary scenes to punctuate this contemporary version of The Thing from Another World . (Directed by John Carpenter, 1982, 109 min., 35mm, Rated R.) Film series: 35mm Screenings / Re-Consider This!. Tickets at nitehawkcinema.com.

events.label: Nitehawk: Agora — Cinema Arabiyya
events.desc: Starring: Neji Kanaweti, Majd Mastoura, Bilel Slatnia, Sonia Zarg Ayouna To make an additional $10 donation to The Sameer Project , select the “Event + Donation” ticket on the checkout screen. In a remote Tunisian town, people who were previously thought to be missing make a sudden return, causing growing tensions within the families, community, and local police. As a result, local police inspector Fathi, with the help of his doctor friend Amine, tries to understand the enigmatic and bizarre circumstances that led to their initial disappearance and unexpected return. As the investigation deepens, a police inspector from the capital, Omar, arrives to solve the mystery. Will Omar’s arrival bring understanding or further complicate matters? (Directed by Ala Eddine Slim, 2024, 102 min., DCP, Rated NR.) Film series: Cinema Arabiyya. Tickets at nitehawkcinema.com.

events.label: Nitehawk: North by Northwest — One Nite Only
events.desc: Starring: Cary Grant, Eva Marie Saint, James Mason, Jessie Royce Landis, Leo G. Carroll, Josephine Hutchinson, Philip Ober, Martin Landau Travel across the country with New York advertising executive Roger O. Thornhill who finds himself on a wild chase filled with murder and intrigue as a crime syndicate mistakenly believes he has the secret microfilm. Add in a sexy blond double (or triple) agent and a stunning score by Bernard Herrmann and you have the makings of classic Hitchcock, his ultimate caper film of mistaken identity starring Cary Grant. (Directed by Alfred Hitchcock, 1959, 136 min., DCP, Rated NR.) Film series: One Nite Only. Tickets at nitehawkcinema.com.

events.label: Nitehawk: The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring — 35mm Screenings
events.desc: Starring: Elijah Wood, Ian McKellen, Liv Tyler, Viggo Mortensen, Sean Astin, Cate Blanchett The future of civilization rests in the fate of the One Ring, which has been lost for centuries. Powerful forces are unrelenting in their search for it. But fate has placed it in the hands of a young Hobbit named Frodo Baggins (Elijah Wood), who inherits the Ring and steps into legend. A daunting task lies ahead for Frodo when he becomes the Ringbearer – to destroy the One Ring in the fires of Mount Doom where it was forged. (Directed by Peter Jackson, 2001, 178 min., 35mm, Rated PG 13.) Film series: 35mm Screenings / The Anniversary Party / Brunch Movies. Tickets at nitehawkcinema.com.

events.label: Nitehawk: Tally Brown, New York — Recent Restorations
events.desc: 2K restoration by the Deutsche Kinemathek “The bewigged Miss Brown, with false eyelashes capable of sending her short, round body aloft, is the most memorable raconteur and cabaret artist you’ll hear all year.” – Melissa Anderson, The Village Voice Both a loving portrait of a larger-than-life personality and a vivid record of New York’s 1970s downtown demimonde, this captivating documentary follows Tally Brown—cabaret chanteuse, underground film star, and a staple of Andy Warhol’s Factory—as she takes filmmaker Rosa von Praunheim on a tour through the grit and glamour of the city that made her. Capturing Brown’s mesmerizing performances (including her breathtaking bilingual cover of David Bowie’s “Heroes”) as well as her social world among fellow queer cult icons like Holly Woodlawn, Divine, and Taylor Mead, Tally Brown, New York is an essential snapshot of a scene that has passed into legend. (Directed by Rosa von Praunheim, 1979, 101 min., DCP, Rated NR.) Film series: Recent Restorations / Representation. Tickets at nitehawkcinema.com.

events.label: Nitehawk: Bugsy — 35mm Screenings
events.desc: Starring: Warren Beatty, Annette Bening, Harvey Keitel, Ben Kingsley, Elliott Gould, Joe Mantegna New York mobster Benjamin Bugsy Siegel (Warren Beatty) leaves New York City to dip into the glamour of Hollywood, Calif., and to build up syndicate gambling rackets. Bowled over by actress Virginia Hill (Annette Bening), the dapper Siegel courts her, despite having a wife and children. Obsessed with creating a gambling haven, Siegel takes racketeering to the Nevada desert and helps develop Las Vegas, only to find himself in deep water over his reckless construction of the Flamingo Hotel. (Directed by Barry Levinson, 1991, 136 min., 35mm, Rated R.) Film series: 35mm Screenings / Best Director, 1991. Tickets at nitehawkcinema.com.

events.label: Nitehawk: Network — The Anniversary Party
events.desc: Starring: Faye Dunaway, Peter Finch, William Holden, Robert Duvall, Beatrice Straight, Wesley Addy, Ned Beatty I’m mad as hell and I’m not going to take this anymore! Fired after twenty-five years as an anchorman on UBS, Howard Beale proclaims on his last broadcast that he was going to commit suicide and, although he doesn’t, his on-air rant of self destruction becomes an unexpected ratings sensation. Fueled by the ambitious programming executive Diana Christensen, the focus of the network takes on a new trashy but lucrative turn that is to the disappointment of the news division president Max Schumacher (Beale’s longtime friend and Christensen’s occasional lover). Forty years after release, Sidney Lumet’s satirical film about the exploitative nature of trash news television is more relevant than ever. (Directed by Sidney Lumet, 1976, 121 min., DCP, Rated R.) Film series: The Anniversary Party. Tickets at nitehawkcinema.com.

events.label: Nitehawk: The Last Waltz — Classic Pictures
events.desc: Seventeen years after joining forces as the backing band for rockabilly cult hero Ronnie Hawkins, Canadian roots rockers The Band call it quits with a lavish farewell show at San Francisco’s Winterland Ballroom on Nov. 25, 1976. Filmed by Martin Scorsese, this documentary features standout performances by rock legends such as Bob Dylan, Van Morrison, Eric Clapton, Joni Mitchell and Muddy Waters, as well as interviews tracing the group’s history and discussing road life. (Directed by Martin Scorsese, 1978, 117 min., DCP, Rated PG.) Film series: Classic Pictures / Brunch Movies. Tickets at nitehawkcinema.com.

events.label: Nitehawk: Beginners — The Anniversary Party
events.desc: Starring: Ewan McGregor, Mélanie Laurent, Christopher Plummer, Goran Visnjic, Mary Page Keller, Kai Lennox Mike Mills’ Beginners imaginatively explores the hilarity, confusion, and surprises of love through the evolving consciousness of Oliver (Ewan McGregor). Oliver meets the irreverent and unpredictable Anna (Mélanie Laurent) only months after his father Hal Fields (Christopher Plummer) has passed away. This new love floods Oliver with memories of his father, who, following the death of his wife of 45 years, came out of the closet at age 75 to live a full, energized, and wonderfully tumultuous gay life – which included a younger boyfriend, Andy (Goran Visnjic). The upheavals of Hal’s new honesty, by turns funny and moving, brought father and son closer than they’d ever been able to be. Now Oliver endeavors to love Anna with all the bravery, humor, and hope that his father taught him. (Directed by Mike Mills, 2010, 105 min., DCP, Rated R.) Film series: The Anniversary Party / Brunch Movies. Tickets at nitehawkcinema.com.

events.label: Nitehawk: Millennium Actress — Anime After Dark
events.desc: Starring: Miyoko Shôji, Shôzô Îzuka, Mami Koyama Experience the gorgeous new restoration of what many believe to be Satoshi Kon’s ( Perfect Blue, Paprika, Tokyo Godfathers ) greatest work, Millennium Actress . When the legendary Ginei Studios shuts down, filmmaker Genya Tachibana and his assistant are tasked with interviewing its reclusive star, Chiyoko Fujiwara, who had retired from the spotlight 30 years prior. As she recounts her career, Genya and his crew are literally pulled into her memories where they witness her chance encounter with a mysterious man on the run from the police. Despite never knowing his name or his face, Chiyoko relentlessly pursues that man in a seamless blend of reality and memory that only Satoshi Kon could deliver. Boasting countless awards, including the Grand Prize in the Japan Agency of Cultural Affairs Media Arts Festival, which it shared with Hayao Miyazaki’s Spirited Away , Millennium Actress is a must-see for anime fans of all ages. (Directed by Satoshi Kon, 2001, 87 min., DCP, Rated PG.) Film series: Anime After Dark / The Anniversary Party. Tickets at nitehawkcinema.com.

events.desc: Starring: Topol, Norma Crane, Leonard Frey, Molly Picon, Paul Mann A lavishly produced and critically acclaimed screen adaptation of the international stage sensation tells the life-affirming story of Tevye, a poor milkman whose love, pride and faith help him face the oppression of turn-of-the-century czarist Russia. (Directed by Norman Jewison, 1971, 181 min., DCP, Rated G.) Film series: Family Friendly / Brunch Movies. Tickets at nitehawkcinema.com.

events.label: Nitehawk: Air Mail — 35mm Screenings
events.desc: Starring: Pat O’Brien, Ralph Bellamy, Gloria Stuart, Slim Summerville, Lilian Bond, Russell Hopton Hosted by Caroline Golum and Cristina Cacioppo Before Howard Hawks’ aviation melodrama Only Angels Have Wings , director John Ford hoisted Depression-era audiences up, up, and away to a cockpit-level view of airmail delivery! Ford’s trademark penchant for the American West provides a perilous backdrop to the surprisingly sensational workaday lives of thrill-junkie postal pilots, centering on a reckless daredevil who won’t let anything – a pal, a dame, or even the Christmas shipping rush! – clip his flight feathers. (Directed by John Ford, 1932, 84 min., 35mm, Rated NR.) Film series: 35mm Screenings / Pre-Code Parade. Tickets at nitehawkcinema.com.

events.label: Nitehawk: Once Upon a Time in Harlem — Adventures in Black Cinema
events.desc: A decade after his death, genre-defying filmmaker William Greaves has one last trick up his sleeve with what he considered the most important event he captured on film: a 1972 party he engineered with the living luminaries of the Harlem Renaissance. For four hours, this extraordinary group – many of whom had not seen each other in fifty years – reminisced, critiqued, argued, laughed and drank while wrestling with their place in a rapidly shifting cultural landscape. Shot on 16mm film, newly restored and now directed by Greaves’ son David, this landmark film is at once a self-exploration and an inquiry into the heart of the critical mass of energy called the Harlem Renaissance. William Greaves’ intent was not only to document these artists and intellectuals as they spoke about their lives and work but also to plumb the meaning of the extraordinary creative period in which they lived to help us better understand how culture has been passed on from one generation to another and the role that the artist plays in keeping it alive. (Directed by David Greaves, 2026, 100 min., DCP, Rated PG 13.) Film series: Adventures in Black Cinema / ICYMI. Tickets at nitehawkcinema.com.

events.label: Nitehawk: Sundays on Fire: Secret Hong Kong 35mm Feature — Sundays on Fire
events.desc: Warning: Images are not from the movies we’re showing. Trust us, you can’t imagine what we’re showing! A career-making film from the late-90s, this caper flick rarely gets screened, but it turned out to be a landmark for both its director and its stars. An anthem to urban loneliness, job dissatisfaction, and unconsummated romance, it’s as light on its feet as Ocean’s 11 , as stylish as North By Northwest , and as heart-achingly emotional as a Cantopop power ballad. Featuring two of Hong Kong’s biggest stars playing lonely men who re-discover their love of life by shooting at each other, it’s a rousing, ridiculous, over-the-top supernova of fun, that reminds us this holiday season that what we have to be thankful for are Hong Kong movies. (93 min., 35mm.) Film series: Sundays on Fire. Tickets at nitehawkcinema.com.

events.label: Bargemusic Concerts
events.desc: For nearly 50 years, Bargemusic has been committed to attracting local audiences and enhancing the cultural life of New York by offering performances of chamber music in an intimate setting – the type of setting in which chamber music is meant to be heard. To make this experience available to as many people as possible, all Bargemusic Concerts are Admission Free. Check the Bargemusic website for details on the performance scheduled for each day. Bargemusic concerts are 1 to 1.5 hours, with no intermission. Doors open 20 minutes before the concert (no tickets, no reservations). No food or drink

events.label: NYP Brooklyn Methodist Hospital Parkinson’s and Other Movement Disorders CME
events.desc: NYP Brooklyn Methodist Hospital Dr. Miran Salgado, Chief of Neurosciences and Dr. Michael Kapplitt, Neurosurgeon at Weill Cornell Medicine Parkinson’s and Other Movement Disorders CME 1st Fridays of the Month / 12pm – 1pm / Zoom Presented by: Dr. Miran Salgado and Dr. Michael Kaplitt CME program will meet on these dates: November 6, December 4, January 1, February 5, March 5, April 2, May 7, June 4 Objectives: At the completion of this activity, participants should be able to: Be able to definitively diagnose Parkinson’s, Parkinsonism, and atypical Parkinson’s DisordersKnow appropriate neurosurgical interventions that are available for treatment of movement disordersRecognize the importance of interdisciplinary team approach and how to utilize the different disciplines to maximize care and treatment for patients with Parkinson’s Disease Target Audience: Physicians in practice, Physician assistants, Physicians in training and Medical Students This activity is sponsored by the Department of Neurosciences. Please contact Rose Brown, LMSW, for Zoom information at eqa9001@nyp.org or 646-704-1792. Accreditation Statement NewYork-Presbyterian Brooklyn Methodist Hospital is accredited by The Medical Society of the State of New York to provide continuing medical education for physicians. New York Presbyterian Brooklyn Methodist Hospital designates this live activity for a maximum of 1 AMA PRA Category 1 Credits™. Physicians should claim only the credit commensurate with the extent of their participation in the activity. Disclosure Statement The Medical Society of The State of New York relies upon planners and faculty participants in its CME activities to provide educational information that is objective and free of bias. In this spirit and in accordance with the guidelines of MSSNY and the ACCME, all speakers and planners for CME activities must disclose any relevant financial relationships with commercial interests whose products, devices or services may be discussed in the content of a CME activity, that might be perceived as a real or apparent conflict of interest. Any discussion of investigational or unlabeled uses of a product will be identified. The planners and faculty participants do not have any financial arrangements or affiliations with any ineligible companies whose products, research or services may be discussed in these materials. Funding Statement No commercial funding has been accepted for the activity.

events.label: Introduction to Birdwatching Outings
events.desc: Whether you’re new to birding or looking to build your skills, this introductory outing is a great way to explore Prospect Park and learn about the birds that visit throughout the year. Join a member of the Brooklyn Bird Club to learn birding basics and search for the dozens of species found in the park across all seasons. All ages and experience levels are welcome. No registration is required. Children under 12 must be accompanied by an adult. What to Bring: Binoculars if you have them, comfortable walking shoes, water, and weather-appropriate clothing. A limited number of binoculars will be available to borrow. Please Note : Pets are not permitted on this outing. Depending on attendance, participants may be divided into smaller groups. Outings are held rain or shine unless severe weather makes conditions unsafe. Route Description: This outing moves at a relaxed pace with frequent stops to observe birds. Routes may vary from week to week depending on bird activity and park conditions. Participants can expect paved paths, dirt trails, grassy areas, slight inclines and occasional steps. The group will cover approximately 1.5–2 miles. Learn more on the Brooklyn Bird Club website.

events.label: Exhibit: The Shirley Chisholm Way: Brooklyn’s Blueprint for Change
events.desc: Join Prospect Park Alliance and Shirley Chisholm Cultural Institute (SCCI) for a new exhibit that explores how Brooklyn’s beloved daughter broke down gender and racial barriers to fight for her community, becoming the first Black woman elected to Congress. The exhibit is organized around seven life lessons drawn from Chisholm’s tenacious career. It features stunning portraits of Chisholm by artist Al Johnson and rarely seen photographs and memorabilia from the Congresswoman’s campaigns, curated by Barbara Bullard, Creative Producer and President of SCCI. These materials offer inspirational insights into how Brooklyn’s beloved daughter broke down gender and racial barriers to become the first Black woman to serve in Congress. This exhibit provides visitors with a space to reflect on Chisholm’s legacy as Prospect Park Alliance welcomes the installation of a new monument in her honor at the Parkside and Ocean Avenue entrance in 2027. The exhibit, curated by Barbara Bullard, Cultural Producer and President of the Shirley Chisholm Cultural Institute, is part of Prospect Park Alliance’s ReImagine Lefferts initiative, which is transforming the museum to explore the legacies of resistance and resilience of the Indigenous people of Lenapehoking, whose unceded ancestral lands the park and house rests upon, and Africans who were enslaved by the Lefferts family. The Shirley Chisholm Cultural Institute (SCCI) has been at the forefront of art, culture, and justice and economic sustainability since 1977, with the official permission and participation of Congresswoman Chisholm herself in its inception and development. events.label: Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit
events.desc: Prospect Park Alliance is collaborating with NewYork-Presbyterian to offer comprehensive sexual health services in Brooklyn’s backyard at Grand Army Plaza every Thursday from 10 am to 3 pm and every Monday at the Parkside + Ocean Avenue Entrance from 10 am to 3 pm. The NewYork-Presbyterian Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit is a safe, inclusive space for people to receive high-quality sexual health services. Learn more about the Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit in Prospect Park or reach out to us at mobilehealth@nyp.org or (929) 923-3543. No insurance or ID is required to receive care. Staffed by a team of NewYork-Presbyterian healthcare providers, the mobile medical unit has an exam room and consult room, and offers routine laboratory testing, vaccinations, and PrEP and PEP medications that lower the risk of HIV infection. Patients can also be connected to social services, benefits enrollment, and local healthcare providers. Other services include sexually transmitted infection (STI) testing, family planning, hepatitis C screening, health education and more. The Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit is made possible through funding from the Dalio Center for Health Justice and the Division of Community and Population Health at NewYork-Presbyterian, and a grant from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.
